seo.title: What is Liquid in Shopify?
seo.description: Liquid is the templating language Shopify themes are written in, which puts store data into the HTML a visitor receives.

definition: Liquid is the templating language Shopify themes are written in, which puts store data into the HTML a visitor receives.
answerBlock: Liquid is the templating language Shopify themes are written in, which puts store data into the HTML a visitor receives. It renders on Shopify's servers, so a Liquid storefront needs no JavaScript to show a product. Sections and blocks written in Liquid are what merchandisers rearrange in the theme editor.

body.heading: What does working in Liquid involve?
paragraphs: Building sections, which are the rearrangeable pieces of a page, and schemas, which decide what a merchandiser may change: a heading, an image, the number of columns, which collection to show. A good theme gives the store team real control without letting them break the layout.

It also means being careful about apps. Many apps install scripts into the theme, and a storefront that started fast can collect a dozen of them within a year. Each one is a decision with a performance cost.
Liquid has limits: it cannot hold complex application logic, and anything genuinely interactive still needs JavaScript or a headless approach.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: A well-built Liquid theme is the cheapest path to a fast, editable shop, and it keeps the store team independent of developers for everyday merchandising.
The commercial trap is the app drawer: every convenience app is a recurring fee and a page-weight cost, and both compound.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: A furniture storefront exposes its collection layout, hero and proof band as editable sections, so a merchandiser can rebuild a seasonal landing page without a deployment.

service.title: Shopify development
service.line: Custom Shopify storefronts, configurators and replatforming for brands that have outgrown a stock theme or a page builder.

terms.definition: Headless commerce keeps the shop engine for products, checkout and payments, but builds the storefront separately on top of its API.
Replatforming is moving a shop or website from one platform to another, taking the data, the addresses and the rankings with it.
